name: Tri Ring Intersecting STorage Accelerators in Nippon
notes: Kondo gives "operation 1986-1995" and "data taking 1987-1995"; the KEK history page gives experiments May 1987 to December 1995. The record uses the KEK history page for the operating interval and the 14 November 1986 date for the first collisions.
The original design (1973) was a three-ring electron-proton facility; only the electron-positron main ring was built in phase 1 (Kondo).

beam_energy.locator: Kondo, section 1 and Table 1 (beam energy 32 GeV)
beam_energy.note: Beam energy reached after the 1988 superconducting-RF upgrade (30 to 32 GeV).
beam_energy.quote: the beam energy from 30 to 32 GeV

circumference.quote: The total circumference was raised to 3016 m

summary.plain: KEK's 3-kilometre electron-positron collider in Tsukuba, Japan, which in November 1986 reached the world's highest collision energy of 50 GeV. Its three detectors AMY, TOPAZ and VENUS searched for the top quark and tested QCD from 1987 to 1995; the tunnel was then reused for KEKB.
summary.technical: TRISTAN e⁺e⁻ main ring (phase 1 of a planned three-ring facility): 3016 m circumference, beam energy 25.5 GeV (1986) rising to 30 GeV (1988, superconducting RF) and 32 GeV; peak luminosity 4.5×10³¹ cm⁻² s⁻¹; approved April 1981, groundbreaking November 1981, first collisions 14 November 1986, experiments May 1987 to December 1995; experiments AMY, TOPAZ, VENUS.
